todos: Adopt greenfield policy across the repository: remove compatibility assumptions for previous image-generation providers, stale settings, migration-style fallback paths, and obsolete user-data preservation logic unless a current feature explicitly needs them.

Remove legacy image-generation settings and UI concepts for external providers such as ComfyUI, Automatic1111, imageGeneration.provider, automatic1111BaseUrl, comfyUiBaseUrl, automatic1111Model, comfyUiWorkflowJson, trustNonLocalEndpoint, and activeExecutionProvider; keep only the integrated local ONNX image engine configuration.

Reset the image-generation data model for the fresh app: define the canonical settings as selectedModelId, requestTimeoutSeconds, and preferGpu; remove code that reads, writes, displays, or attempts to recover removed image-provider settings.

Verify the integrated image-generation catalog entries on the target machine: SDXL Base qualita for portraits/people, SDXL Turbo rapido for fast drafts, LCM SDXL bozza for prompt iteration, and FFusionXL creativo for illustration-oriented prompts.

Measure the new quality-to-speed image preset mapping per model: Qualita, Bilanciato, and Velocita must produce acceptable latency, memory use, prompt adherence, and fewer human anatomy failures on DirectML.

Tune model-specific generation defaults after real outputs are reviewed: keep Turbo/LCM at low guidance and low steps, keep base SDXL models at higher guidance, and adjust step counts only when visual quality improves.

Centralize remaining image UI help text into compact tooltips: model choice, preset slider, format, seed, negative prompt, download consent, and catalog editor should avoid long visible explanatory paragraphs.

Remove or hide remaining raw image parameters from the primary workflow: step count, batch size, exact dimensions, negative prompt, and seed should stay behind presets or advanced controls unless direct editing is necessary.

Harden model verification before generation: verify the selected snapshot has every required file, reject placeholder files, reject unsupported model_index.json pipeline classes with a clear model-not-ready error, and avoid reporting the engine as ready for an incompatible model layout.

Simplify the image engine provider flow: prefer DirectML on Windows when preferGpu is true, fall back to CPU only after a real DirectML initialization failure, and remove any separate NVIDIA/CUDA image-provider selection path from API, UI text, docs, and tests.

Make runtime packaging deterministic for Windows: ensure desktop debug, publish, and installer outputs are runtime-specific win-x64 by default and include the native ONNX Runtime files needed by the DirectML package.

Replace image-generation unexpected 500 errors with typed user-facing failures where practical: model incompatible, model incomplete, DirectML unavailable, CPU fallback failed, timeout, and generated output missing.

Prune obsolete local-state assumptions from tests: update API and web tests so they assert the new greenfield image settings, DirectML wording, model verification behavior, and removal of external-provider configuration.

Update docs and README for the new app posture: describe OnlyRag as a fresh integrated-local app, remove legacy provider setup instructions, clarify DirectML-on-NVIDIA behavior, and keep only current setup and troubleshooting paths.

Review installer and bootstrap copy for stale compatibility language: remove references to external image providers, legacy endpoints, or migration behavior; keep explicit consent for integrated model downloads and Windows DirectML requirements.

Run full repository verification after cleanup: dotnet test for all .NET test projects, web lint/typecheck/test/build, installer prerequisite checks, and any packaging checks that are available locally.

Manually verify integrated image generation on the target NVIDIA machine after cleanup: model download, snapshot verification, runtime status showing DirectML before generation, prompt generation, saved gallery entry, generated file retrieval, and no fallbackReason unless DirectML actually fails.

Manually verify CPU image fallback after cleanup by disabling GPU preference or forcing a DirectML initialization failure, then confirm runtime status shows CPU with a clear fallbackReason and generation still saves retrievable images.

Run representative runtime workflows on the target deployment scope after legacy removal: real OCR on scanned PDF/image with NVIDIA runtime and CPU fallback, real Qdrant document import/search/chat indexing, Ollama chat/embedding/translation using chosen local models, and LibreOffice PDF translation export.

Monitor and add the next OCR NVIDIA CUDA runtime target beyond cuda130 only when PaddlePaddle publishes stable Windows win_amd64 paddlepaddle-gpu wheels for newer CUDA SDK targets such as cu132 or cu133; update runtime-manifest.json, requirements-nvidia-cu*.txt, Test-OcrRuntimeCatalog.ps1, then verify the installed app provisions and uses the new GPU runtime successfully.
